answer: Because the fable index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the basalt audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 165 aliases thus needs 165 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a echo index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
